cards.b:
Hotspot questions appear again and again: how many are in India, which hotspot covers which state, and what the criteria are. Mains also asks whether hotspot thinking helps or hurts conservation.

Know the criteria, the four Indian hotspots and what each one holds.

A frequent trap: the Eastern Ghats and the Western Ghats are often swapped in options.

The idea was proposed by Norman Myers in 1988. Conservation International later adopted and refined it. A region is a hotspot if it:

  • has at least 1,500 endemic vascular plant species (over 0.5 percent of the world total); and
  • has lost at least 70 percent of its original natural vegetation.

World total is 36 hotspots (as of the 2016 update). They cover about 2.5 percent of land but hold over half of the world's endemic plants.

India has four hotspots, partly or wholly inside its borders.

  • Himalaya: the Himalayan arc across Bhutan, Nepal and north India.
  • Indo-Burma: includes north-east India (outside the Himalaya) and Myanmar, Thailand and others.
  • Western Ghats and Sri Lanka: the Western Ghats were named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012.
  • Sundaland: includes the Nicobar Islands.

The Eastern Ghats are not a hotspot.

The Western Ghats are home to the lion-tailed macaque, Nilgiri tahr and Malabar civet. The Himalaya holds the red panda, snow leopard and Himalayan monal. Indo-Burma has the hoolock gibbon (India's only ape) and many orchids. The Nicobars have the Nicobar megapode and giant robber crab.

Endemism is the key. A species found only in one area, and lost there, is lost to the world.

The 17 mega-diverse countries were named by Conservation International and UNEP-WCMC (1998). They hold about 70 percent of world biodiversity. India is one. Others include Brazil, Indonesia, Colombia, China, Australia, Mexico and South Africa.

A country can be mega-diverse without being a hotspot, and a hotspot can cross many countries. Do not confuse the two.

Other ways to rank conservation areas:

  • Global 200 ecoregions (WWF).
  • Endemic Bird Areas (BirdLife).
  • Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas (IBAs). India has over 500.
  • Key Biodiversity Areas.
  • Frontier forests and high-biodiversity wilderness areas.

Hotspots focus on threat plus endemism. Wilderness areas focus on intact, low-threat regions.

Supporters say hotspots give clear priorities and attract funding, such as the Critical Ecosystem Partnership Fund. Critics say they ignore vast low-endemism ecosystems like savannas, ignore animals, and may neglect the poor who live inside them. A few say the 70 percent loss test rewards areas that are already damaged.

A balanced answer: hotspots are a triage tool, not a full strategy.

Threats include dams, mining, monoculture plantations, shifting cultivation in the North-East, and tourism pressure. The Western Ghats Ecology Expert Panel (Gadgil, 2011) and the High-Level Working Group (Kasturirangan, 2013) debated how much to protect.

Responses: protected areas, biosphere reserves such as Nilgiri and Nokrek, and the Biological Diversity Act 2002. Climate change adds new pressure on mountain species.

• Criteria: 1,500 endemic plants, 70 percent loss.
  • World hotspots: 36.
  • India: 4 (Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats and Sri Lanka, Sundaland).
  • Mega-diverse countries: 17.

If a question gives a species and asks for its hotspot, think of its habitat first. The hoolock gibbon points to Indo-Burma.

Prelims-style: "Consider the following statements on biodiversity hotspots" with the two criteria. Remember that endemism and habitat loss are both needed.

Mains-style: "What are biodiversity hotspots? Discuss the conservation challenges of India's hotspots." Structure: define; criteria; four Indian hotspots; threats; policy; way forward.

Remember also that hotspots are about plants and endemism, so a hotspot does not automatically have the most animals or the most forest cover.

quiz.q: Who proposed the biodiversity hotspot concept in 1988?
quiz.w: Myers proposed it; Conservation International refined it.

quiz.q: A hotspot needs at least how many endemic vascular plants?
quiz.w: Plus loss of 70 percent of original vegetation.

quiz.q: Which is NOT a hotspot covering Indian territory?
quiz.w: The Eastern Ghats are not a hotspot.

quiz.q: The Nicobar Islands belong to which hotspot?
How many hotspots exist worldwide as of the 2016 update?
quiz.w: The list grew from 25 to 34 to 36.

quiz.q: Which animal is India's only ape?
quiz.w: Found in Indo-Burma, in the North-East.

quiz.q: The Western Ghats became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:
quiz.w: Inscribed in 2012 as a serial site.

quiz.q: How many mega-diverse countries are recognised?
Which group named the Global 200 ecoregions?
quiz.w: Also see Endemic Bird Areas by BirdLife.
It lives in the high grasslands of Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
